subject.title: fix(agents): repair orphaned tool_use pairs on compaction prune path

question: Should built-in compaction drop aborted assistant tool-call turns before summarization, matching prompt-send sanitizer behavior, or should it preserve them by synthesizing an explicit result?
rationale: Both choices are technically plausible and affect session-state semantics; automation should not choose whether losing the interrupted assistant attempt is preferable to fabricating a result in compaction summaries.

options.title: Accept drop policy
options.body: Merge the focused repair and accept small context loss for aborted tool-call turns to prevent strict-provider transcript rejection.

options.title: Require synthetic result policy
options.body: Ask the contributor to preserve aborted turns with an explicit synthetic or unknown-result representation and add matching compaction tests.

options.title: Defer broader recovery design
options.body: Keep this PR paused while maintainers design a richer transcript recovery policy that covers built-in and pluggable compaction providers together.

recommendation.title: Accept drop policy
recommendation.body: Merge the focused repair and accept small context loss for aborted tool-call turns to prevent strict-provider transcript rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-transcript-repair ownership makes this the best available routing candidate for the drop-versus-synthesize policy choice.
